preconditions.description: The number of vertices n and the number of edges m must be within the specified range.

postconditions.description: The output must either be 'Impossible' or start with 'Possible\n' followed by the edges.
If the output is possible, it must contain exactly m + 1 lines after 'Possible'.

postconditions.expression: return_value.startswith('Possible\n') implies all(1 <= int(edge.split()[0]) <= n and 1 <= int(edge.split()[1]) <= n and int(edge.split()[0]) != int(edge.split()[1]) for edge in return_value.split('\n')[1:])
postconditions.description: Each edge must have valid vertex numbers and cannot be a self-loop.

postconditions.expression: return_value.startswith('Possible\n') implies all(gcd(int(edge.split()[0]), int(edge.split()[1])) == 1 for edge in return_value.split('\n')[1:])
postconditions.description: Each edge must have vertices that are relatively prime.

postconditions.expression: return_value.startswith('Possible\n') implies len(set(tuple(sorted(edge.split())) for edge in return_value.split('\n')[1:])) == m
postconditions.description: There must be exactly m unique edges.

postconditions.expression: return_value.startswith('Possible\n') implies all(any(int(edge.split()[0]) in path and int(edge.split()[1]) in path for path in paths) for edge in return_value.split('\n')[1:])
